# Increase default timeout and retry behavior

Source: https://github.com/vanshbordia/vlrdevapi/blob/main/betterdocs/content/docs/config.mdx

title: Configuration
description: Configure base URL, timeouts, user agent, retries, backoff, and rate limiting at runtime

import { Steps } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';

## Overview

The global configuration lets you control core runtime behavior across the library:

- Base URL
- Default timeout
- Default User-Agent
- Retries and backoff
- Built-in rate limiting

Changes take effect immediately and apply across modules like `fetcher`, `events`, `series`, `matches`, `players`, `teams`, and `search`.

## Types

Below are the core configuration fields and helper functions with their Python types.

### Configuration fields

    vlr_base: {
      type: 'str',
      description: 'Base URL for VLR.gg requests',
      default: '"https://www.vlr.gg"',
    default_timeout: {
      description: 'Default HTTP timeout (seconds) for requests',
    default_user_agent: {
      type: 'str',
      description: 'Default User-Agent header used by the fetcher',
      default: 'Chrome-like UA',
    max_retries: {
      description: 'Maximum number of retries for transient errors',
      default: '3',
    backoff_factor: {
      description: 'Exponential backoff multiplier between retries',
      default: '1.0',
    default_rate_limit: {
      description: 'Default requests-per-second (RPS) when rate limiting is enabled',
      default: '10',
    default_rate_limit_enabled: {
      type: 'bool',
      description: 'Whether built-in rate limiting is enabled by default',
      default: 'true',
  title="Global configuration fields"
  description="Values can be changed at runtime via vlr.configure(...) and restored with vlr.reset_config()"

### Helper functions

    configure: {
      type: 'function',
      description: 'Update one or more global configuration values at runtime',
      params: [
        { name: 'vlr_base', type: 'str | None', required: false },
        { name: 'default_timeout', type: 'float | None', required: false },
        { name: 'default_user_agent', type: 'str | None', required: false },
        { name: 'max_retries', type: 'int | None', required: false },
        { name: 'backoff_factor', type: 'float | None', required: false },
        { name: 'default_rate_limit', type: 'float | None', required: false },
        { name: 'default_rate_limit_enabled', type: 'bool | None', required: false },
      ],
      returns: { type: 'None' },
    reset_config: {
      type: 'function',
      description: 'Reset all configuration values to library defaults',
      returns: { type: 'None' },
    configure_rate_limit: {
      type: 'function',
      description: 'Temporarily override current rate limiting behavior',
      params: [
        { name: 'requests_per_second', type: 'float | None', required: false },
        { name: 'enabled', type: 'bool | None', required: false },
      ],
      returns: { type: 'None' },
    reset_rate_limit: {
      type: 'function',
      description: 'Reset rate limit to current configured defaults',
      returns: { type: 'None' },
    get_rate_limit: {
      type: 'function',
      description: 'Get current RPS; returns 0.0 when disabled',
      returns: { type: 'float' },
  title="Helpers"
  description="Available functions for configuring global behavior and rate limiting"

## Quick Examples

### Increase timeout and retries

```python
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Increase default timeout and retry behavior
vlr.configure(default_timeout=10.0, max_retries=5, backoff_factor=2.0)

# Calls now use the new defaults
events = vlr.events.list_events(limit=5)
```

### Custom User-Agent

```python
import vlrdevapi as vlr

vlr.configure(default_user_agent="MyApp/1.0 (+https://example.com)")
```

### Change base URL (advanced)

```python
import vlrdevapi as vlr

vlr.configure(vlr_base="https://my-proxy.example.com")
```

## Rate Limiting

The client uses a lightweight token-bucket limiter. You can change whether it is enabled and what rate to use.

```python
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Disable
vlr.configure(default_rate_limit_enabled=False)

# Enable and set to 20 requests per second
vlr.configure(default_rate_limit=20, default_rate_limit_enabled=True)

# Temporarily override at runtime via fetcher helpers
vlr.configure_rate_limit(requests_per_second=5, enabled=True)

# Reset back to configured defaults
vlr.reset_rate_limit()
```

## Reset to defaults

```python
import vlrdevapi as vlr

vlr.reset_config()
```

## Per-call overrides

You can still override settings per-call on `fetcher` functions.

```python
from vlrdevapi.fetcher import fetch_html

# Override timeout just for this request
html = fetch_html("https://www.vlr.gg/matches", timeout=2.5)
```

## Related

    href="/docs/rate-limiting"
    title="Rate Limiting"
    description="Control request throughput globally or at runtime"
    href="/docs/getting-started"
    title="Quick Start"
    description="Install and make your first requests"

# Check if VLR.gg is reachable

Source: https://github.com/vanshbordia/vlrdevapi/blob/main/betterdocs/content/docs/getting-started.mdx

title: Getting Started
description: Learn the basics of using vlrdevapi

import { Steps, Step } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';
import { Tabs, Tab } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';
import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

This guide walks you through the common flows with `vlrdevapi`.

<Steps>
<Step>

## Install the Package

```bash title="Install via pip"
pip install vlrdevapi
```

Or with uv:

```bash title="Install via uv"
uv add vlrdevapi
```

</Step>

<Step>

## Import and Verify

```python title="Quick Verification"
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Check if VLR.gg is reachable
if vlr.status.check_status():
    print("Ready to use vlrdevapi!")
else:
    print("VLR.gg is currently unreachable")
```

</Step>

<Step>

## Your First Query

<Tabs items={['Matches', 'Search', 'Events']}>
<Tab value="Matches">

```python title="Get Upcoming Matches"
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Get next 5 upcoming matches
matches = vlr.matches.upcoming(limit=5)

for m in matches:
    print(f"{m.event} - {m.event_phase}")
    print(f"  {m.team1.name} vs {m.team2.name}")
    print(f"  Time: {m.time}")
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Search">

```python title="Search for Teams and Players"
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Search across all categories
results = vlr.search.search('sentinels')

print(f"Found {results.total_results} results:")
print(f"  Players: {len(results.players)}")
print(f"  Teams: {len(results.teams)}")
print(f"  Events: {len(results.events)}")
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Events">

```python title="List Ongoing Events"
import vlrdevapi as vlr
from vlrdevapi.events import EventTier, EventStatus

# Get ongoing VCT events
events = vlr.events.list_events(
    tier=EventTier.VCT,
    status=EventStatus.ONGOING,
    limit=5
)

for e in events:
    print(f"{e.name} - {e.prize or 'TBD'}")
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step>

## Rate Limiting

By default, vlrdevapi limits requests to **10 per second**. Adjust if needed:

```python title="Configure Rate Limiting"
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Check current RPS (0.0 means disabled)
print(vlr.get_rate_limit())

# Set to 5 requests/second (enabled)
vlr.configure_rate_limit(requests_per_second=5.0, enabled=True)

# Disable temporarily (not recommended)
vlr.configure_rate_limit(enabled=False)

# Restore default (10 req/s, enabled)
vlr.reset_rate_limit()
```

<Callout type="info" title="Recommended Settings">
Keep rate limiting enabled. The default of 10 requests/second is a good balance for most use cases.
</Callout>

</Step>

# Upcoming matches

Source: https://github.com/vanshbordia/vlrdevapi/blob/main/betterdocs/content/docs/index.mdx

title: VLR Dev API
description: A clean Python client for Valorant esports data from VLR.gg

import { GithubInfo } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/github-info';
import { BookOpen, Rocket, Search, Users, Trophy, Video, Shield, Signal, Code2 } from 'lucide-react';

## Welcome

VLR Dev API is a typed Python client for Valorant esports data scraped from VLR.gg.

- Typed models with safe defaults
- Consistent, human-friendly function signatures
- Null-safe examples and clear error handling
- Built-in rate limiting (10 req/s default, configurable)

## Quick Start

```python title="Quick Start"
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Upcoming matches
matches = vlr.matches.upcoming(limit=5)
for m in matches:
    print(m.event, '-', m.team1.name, 'vs', m.team2.name)
```

## Example: End-to-end

```python title="Lookup a team and upcoming matches"
import vlrdevapi as vlr

team = vlr.teams.info(team_id=1034)
if team:
    roster = vlr.teams.roster(team.team_id)
    upcoming = vlr.teams.upcoming_matches(team.team_id, limit=2)

    print(f"{team.name} ({team.tag}) - {team.country}")
    print(f"Roster: {len(roster)} players")

    print("\nNext matches:")
    for match in upcoming:
        print(f"  {match.tournament_name}: {match.team1.name} vs {match.team2.name}")
```

# or

Source: https://github.com/vanshbordia/vlrdevapi/blob/main/betterdocs/content/docs/installation.mdx

title: Installation
description: Install and set up vlrdevapi for Python

## Requirements

- Python 3.11+
- pip or uv/poetry

## Install

```bash
pip install vlrdevapi
# or
uv add vlrdevapi
```

## Verify

```python
import vlrdevapi as vlr
print(vlr.__version__)

# Optional: check site reachability (if using the status helper)
try:
    from vlrdevapi import status
    print(status.check_status())
except Exception:
    # status helper may not be available in all builds
    pass
```

If the status helper (when available) returns `False`, VLR.gg may be down or blocked.

## Optional: Configure Rate Limiting

```python
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Check current RPS (0.0 means disabled)
print(vlr.get_rate_limit())

# Set to 5 requests/second and enable
vlr.configure_rate_limit(requests_per_second=5.0, enabled=True)

# Restore defaults (10 req/s, enabled)
vlr.reset_rate_limit()
```

See: [Rate Limiting](/docs/rate-limiting)

---

# Get current RPS (0.0 means disabled)

Source: https://github.com/vanshbordia/vlrdevapi/blob/main/betterdocs/content/docs/rate-limiting.mdx

title: Rate Limiting
description: Configure request rate limiting for vlrdevapi

vlrdevapi provides a built-in, global rate limiter so you can avoid overwhelming VLR.gg and reduce 429 errors.

## Default

- Enabled by default
- Requests per second (RPS): 10

## API

```python title="Public helpers"
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Get current RPS (0.0 means disabled)
current = vlr.get_rate_limit()

# Change RPS and enable/disable
vlr.configure_rate_limit(requests_per_second=5.0, enabled=True)
vlr.configure_rate_limit(enabled=False)  # disable

# Restore defaults (10 RPS, enabled)
vlr.reset_rate_limit()
```

## Examples

```python title="Lower rate for sensitive flows"
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Temporarily reduce to 3 RPS
vlr.configure_rate_limit(requests_per_second=3.0, enabled=True)

# ... do your calls ...

# Restore defaults
vlr.reset_rate_limit()
```

```python title="Disable briefly (not recommended)"
import vlrdevapi as vlr

# Disable limiter (0.0 when disabled)
vlr.configure_rate_limit(enabled=False)
print(vlr.get_rate_limit())  # 0.0

# Re-enable at 10 RPS
vlr.reset_rate_limit()
```

## Error Handling

- The limiter is applied automatically by all network calls.
- When disabled, no waiting is applied.
- If VLR.gg responds with HTTP 429, a `RateLimitError` is raised.
